Xavier Becerra

Democratic candidate for Governor, California · Open seat

Former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services; former California Attorney General

Xavier Becerra is a Democrat from Sacramento. He served in Congress representing Los Angeles, then as California Attorney General, then as U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services under President Biden. He advanced from the top-two primary and faces Republican Steve Hilton in the November 3, 2026 general election to succeed Gov. Gavin Newsom, who is termed out.

Where Becerra stands

Cost of living / utilities and insurance
Says he will declare a state of emergency to freeze insurance and utility rates, and wants to crack down on what he considers price gouging.
Taxes
Supports a progressive income tax and extending a higher tax rate on high earners to pay for schools. Opposes Proposition 40, the billionaire wealth tax. Has not ruled out raising taxes.
Housing
Would declare a state of emergency to fund 40,000 already-approved affordable housing units, push cities to zone for more housing, expand down payment assistance, and limit large corporations from buying homes in bulk.
Climate and energy
Says he supports the state's clean energy transition goals but is open to revising them, including the 2035 ban on sales of new gas cars, if gas and energy become unaffordable.
Homelessness
Would create an ongoing state funding stream for rental assistance and homelessness prevention, plus a public dashboard tracking state-funded units. Says people should not be allowed to stay on the street when offered shelter.
Federal relations / Trump administration
Points to his record of suing the first Trump administration more than 100 times as attorney general. Says he would take a similar approach as governor on issues such as immigration and environmental policy.
Public safety
Voted for Proposition 36 (2024). Says he would fully fund its provisions and make sure defendants receive court-mandated drug treatment to avoid jail time.
Health care
Says he will protect Californians from federal Medicaid cuts.

Background

  • U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2021–2025), under President Joe Biden
  • California Attorney General (2017–2021), appointed in 2017
  • U.S. Representative from Los Angeles (more than two decades, before 2017)
  • Former deputy attorney general, California Department of Justice (late 1980s)
  • Former administrative assistant to state Sen. Art Torres
  • B.A. and J.D., Stanford University
  • Born and raised in Sacramento
